title: Orbit and Horizon
premise: Felix Zhou, navigator of the salvage freighter Vesper's Lantern, keeps a private log of Meridian Colony's slow abandonment while the ship's hold holds illegal memory-backups of colonists who paid to be 'kept safe' from a war that never came. When a research vessel returns from deep space carrying a crew biologically aged backward, the Lantern's crew learns the backups are not copies but anchors—evidence that someone has been harvesting human memory to power a forbidden FTL relay at the edge of dead space. Pursued by the Concordance fleet that erased Meridian from every chart, Felix must carry the backups to the relay and choose between broadcasting the truth, which will doom the colony's survivors, and destroying the relay, which will erase the backups—and the last living record of everyone he loved. He broadcasts it, at the cost of his own memories, and the novel ends with a stranger reading Felix's log and deciding to remember him.
about_author: Casper Eriksen is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade relaying messages between ships that rarely answered. They write about people who keep records no one asked for, from a coastal town whose name they decline to share.

chapters.title: The Hold Full of Sleepers
chapters.summary: Felix Zhou's POV. A routine cargo run to dying Meridian Colony; Felix records the colony's empty streets and checks on the forty-one memory-backups stored illegally in the hold. Establishes his ritual of logging what others ignore. Emotional beat: quiet grief disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Charts That Forget
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The Lantern's captain, Ilsa Voss, discovers Meridian has been scrubbed from official shipping charts. Felix realizes someone is erasing the colony deliberately, not just neglecting it. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into dread.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Remembers Twice
chapters.summary: POV: Sef, a fourteen-year-old Meridian straggler who smuggled herself aboard. She recognizes Felix from a memory she shouldn't have—his own, from a backup session. Emotional beat: uncanny intimacy; Felix begins questioning what the backups actually contain.

chapters.title: Signal from Dead Space
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The Lantern intercepts a distress transmission from the research vessel Anthea, returning from a nine-year deep-space survey. Ilsa orders them to answer despite the risk. Emotional beat: the pull of obligation versus self-preservation.

chapters.title: Aged Backward
chapters.summary: POV: Dr. Amara Osei, the Anthea's xenobiologist, now biologically twenty-five though she remembers sixty years. She describes the anomaly her crew found near the relay: a region where time runs in reverse for organic matter. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The Concordance Arrives
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A Concordance patrol ship demands the Lantern surrender the Anthea's crew. Ilsa refuses and burns hard for the colony's shadow, buying hours. Emotional beat: defiance, and the first open violence of the story.

chapters.title: What the Backups Dream
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef sneaks into the hold and touches a backup cradle, experiencing fragments of forty-one lives at once—including a memory of the relay being built by colonists who were told it was a weather station. Emotional beat: revelation through overwhelming empathy.

chapters.title: The Price List
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix finds the original contracts: colonists sold their memories to fund the relay, believing the backups would be returned. The Concordance kept them as leverage. Emotional beat: betrayal; the theme of power's corruption made concrete.

chapters.title: Meridian's Last Vote
chapters.summary: POV: Elder Tomas Reyes, the colony's dying leader. He gathers the remaining two hundred colonists and reveals he signed the contracts, trading their memories for survival during the war scare. Emotional beat: confession, and a community choosing to face erasure with open eyes.

chapters.title: Burned Orbit
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The Concordance fires on Meridian's orbital tether to destroy evidence. The Lantern rescues survivors in a desperate low-orbit run; Ilsa is gravely injured. Emotional beat: the cost of staying invisible finally coming due.

chapters.title: The Anthea's Secret
chapters.summary: POV: Amara Osei. She confesses the survey was Concordance-funded to test memory-harvesting as FTL fuel; her reversed aging is a failed experiment. The relay doesn't transmit—it consumes. Emotional beat: complicity and the hunger to make amends.

chapters.title: Sef's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef offers herself as a living anchor—the backups respond to her hybrid memory—to help Felix navigate dead space, where instruments fail but memory holds true. Emotional beat: a child claiming agency in a war she inherited.

chapters.title: Into the Quiet
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The Lantern crosses into dead space. Navigation fails; Felix steers by memories Sef channels from the backups, flying through other people's pasts. Emotional beat: trust, and the strange beauty of shared memory.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: POV: Amara. They reach the relay: a cathedral of black lattice feeding on stored human memory, still growing. Amara realizes destroying it will kill the backups; broadcasting through it will expose the Concordance but paint a target on every survivor. Emotional beat: the impossible choice stated plainly.

chapters.title: Concordance Trap
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The fleet arrives, having tracked them. An admiral offers amnesty for the backups and the Anthea's data—proof the Concordance will keep harvesting. Ilsa, dying, tells Felix amnesty is just a quieter erasure. Emotional beat: temptation, and refusal.

chapters.title: What Ilsa Kept
chapters.summary: POV: Ilsa Voss, in her final hours. She reveals she took the backup contract years ago to save her own crew, and has been hiding her guilt ever since; Felix is her attempt at restitution. Emotional beat: forgiveness offered too late to matter, and mattering anyway.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix feeds the backups and the colony's records into the relay and transmits everything to every open channel. The relay overloads, consuming memories as fuel—including, as Amara warned, Felix's own. Emotional beat: climax; sacrifice rendered as a fading first-person log.

chapters.title: Empty Rooms
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The relay dies; the fleet, exposed, scatters. Sef finds Felix alive but hollow—he no longer knows her name. She begins reading his log to him, rebuilding him entry by entry. Emotional beat: devastation answered by devotion.

chapters.title: The Colony That Wouldn't Be Forgotten
chapters.summary: POV: Tomas Reyes. Across human space, Meridian's records go viral; colonies that sold memories rise up. Tomas watches the news from a hospital bed, finally at peace. Emotional beat: vindication without triumph.

chapters.title: What Felix Forgot
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef discovers the backups' final fragments survived inside her, including Felix's own stored memory. She can restore some of him—but each fragment she returns, she loses from herself. Emotional beat: love measured in mutual diminishment.

chapters.title: Horizon
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, fragmentary. Partially restored, Felix chooses not to take back everything, leaving room for who he might become. He and Sef pilot the Lantern away from dead space toward an uncharted star. Emotional beat: bittersweet renewal; memory as a choice, not a possession.

chapters.title: The Reader
chapters.summary: POV: an unnamed archivist, years later. She finds Felix's original log in a recovered archive, reads it through the night, and adds her own entry: a promise that someone, somewhere, will always remember. Emotional beat: resolution; the novel itself becomes the backup.
